claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Unity Catalog's semantic layer combines metric views, which are reusable SQL objects separating measures from dimensions and materializing for performance, with a business-semantics and agent-metadata layer that makes definitions legible to BI tools, SQL, and AI agents.
claims.quote: Unity Catalog's semantic layer combines metric views, reusable SQL objects that separate measures from dimensions and materialize them for performance, with a business-semantics and agent-metadata layer that makes those definitions legible to BI tools, SQL, and AI agents like Genie.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A metric view defines a calculation once, lets any query group by whichever dimension it needs, and materializes the result so repeated queries do not re-scan underlying tables.
claims.quote: A metric view defines the calculation once and lets any query group by whatever dimension it needs, then materializes the result so repeated queries don’t re-scan the underlying tables.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Business semantics and agent metadata supply synonyms, display names, and formatting so agents can interpret a metric correctly.
claims.quote: Business semantics and agent metadata: synonyms, display names, and formatting that make a metric legible to Genie and other agents.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A context layer sits above the set of platform-specific semantic layers and keeps a metric such as revenue consistent across Databricks Genie and dbt-based agents.
claims.quote: It sits above the whole set, keeping “revenue” consistent whether the question comes from Genie inside Databricks or an agent working against dbt on the other side of the estate.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Metric definitions are queryable from outside Databricks via MCP, SQL, and APIs, but the definitions themselves are not yet portable.
claims.quote: Metrics are queryable via MCP, SQL, and APIs from outside Databricks, but the definitions themselves are not yet portable.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Metric views inherit Unity Catalog's existing governance rather than creating a separate parallel governance system.
claims.quote: Metric views don’t create a parallel governance system; they inherit the one Unity Catalog already has.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Unity Catalog supports attribute-based access control in beta and full read/write governance for Apache Iceberg tables on par with Delta Lake.
claims.quote: Unity Catalog now supports attribute-based access control in beta, alongside “full read/write governance support for Apache Iceberg tables, on par with Delta Lake.”
